title: Cohomology and canonical degree-zero comparison of a total left derived functor on objects
statement:
Let $\mathcal A,\mathcal B$ be abelian categories [def-sp-abelian]. Suppose $\mathcal A$ has enough projectives, meaning that every object admits an epimorphism from an object $P$ for which every morphism $P\to Y$ lifts along every epimorphism $X\to Y$. Let $V:\mathcal A\to\mathcal B$ be additive and right exact, meaning that it preserves cokernels and finite direct sums. Write $Q_{\mathcal A}:K(\mathcal A)\to D(\mathcal A)$ and $Q_{\mathcal B}:K(\mathcal B)\to D(\mathcal B)$ for the localizations at quasi-isomorphisms [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], and let $K(V)$ apply $V$ termwise. Assume that the total left derived functor of $Q_{\mathcal B}K(V)$ is defined at every object: for each $C\in K(\mathcal A)$ the diagram $(s:C'\to C)\mapsto Q_{\mathcal B}V(C')$ over quasi-isomorphisms into $C$ is essentially constant as in [def-pur-saturated-triangulated-localization]. Denote its value by $LV(Q_{\mathcal A}C)$ and its canonical natural comparison by $\varepsilon_C:LV(Q_{\mathcal A}C)\to Q_{\mathcal B}V(C)$. For $M\in\mathcal A$, put $T^q(M)=H^q(LV(Q_{\mathcal A}(M[0])))$, where $M[0]$ is concentrated in degree zero. Then $T^q(M)=0$ for every $q>0$, and the canonical map
$$c_M=H^0(\varepsilon_{M[0]}):T^0(M)\longrightarrow V(M)$$
(using $H^0(Q_{\mathcal B}(V(M)[0]))\cong V(M)$) is an isomorphism. These maps are natural: $c_N\circ T^0(f)=V(f)\circ c_M$ for every $f:M\to N$. Moreover $\varepsilon_{M[0]}$ is an isomorphism if and only if $T^q(M)=0$ for every $q<0$.

source.place: Duals of Tag 05TC (lemma-negative-vanishing), Tag 05TD (lemma-left-exact-higher-derived), and Tag 015C (lemma-F-acyclic); Tag 05T5 (lemma-irrelevant), clauses (3) and (4), compares unbounded and bounded-above left derivation on M[0]. Naturality is that of the canonical comparison.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-subcategory-left-resolution] to $K=M[0]$, bound $0$ and $\mathcal P$ the projectives: $P^q$ is projective, $P^q=0$ for $q>0$, and $a:P\to M[0]$ is a quasi-isomorphism; put $p_0=a^0$. As $P^1=0$, $H^0(a):\operatorname{Coker}(d^{-1})\to M$ is invertible, so $p_0$ is a cokernel of $d^{-1}$. By [lem-sc-bounded-above-projective-kprojective], chain maps from $P$ to acyclic complexes (degree-zero cocycles of the Hom complex) are null-homotopic ($dh+hd$), so $1_P$ is initial in $S/P$ by [lem-trf-kprojective-denominator-initial].

source.place: Tag 0646 (lemma-projective-resolutions-exist) for the resolution; dual of Tag 05TH (lemma-injective-acyclic) and Definition 05S9 for the initial denominator.

proof.text: For $F=Q_{\mathcal B}K(V)$, the given essential-value cone has legs $u_s=\varepsilon_Y LV(Q_{\mathcal A}s)^{-1}$. Thus $u_{1_P}=\varepsilon_P$, which is invertible by [lem-trf-essential-pro-initial-evaluation]. Since $a$ is a quasi-isomorphism, $LV(Q_{\mathcal A}a)$ is invertible. Define the derived-category isomorphism $i_M=\varepsilon_P\circ LV(Q_{\mathcal A}a)^{-1}:LV(Q_{\mathcal A}(M[0]))\xrightarrow{\sim}Q_{\mathcal B}V(P)$. Naturality of the given comparison at $a$ says $\varepsilon_{M[0]}\circ LV(Q_{\mathcal A}a)=Q_{\mathcal B}V(a)\circ\varepsilon_P$. Multiplication by the inverse gives the precise normalization $\varepsilon_{M[0]}=Q_{\mathcal B}V(a)\circ i_M$.

source.place: Tag 05TH, lemma-injective-acyclic, dual projective-resolution computation; naturality of the canonical comparison from Definition Tag 05S9.

proof.text: Additivity sends a zero object to a zero object: $1_{V(0)}=V(1_0)=V(0)=0$. Hence $V(P)^q=0$ for $q>0$. The kernel/image definition gives $H^q(V(P))=0$ in these degrees, so applying $H^q$ to $i_M$ proves $T^q(M)=0$ for every $q>0$. In degree zero, $d^0_{V(P)}=0$, whence $H^0(V(P))=\operatorname{Coker}(V(d^{-1}))$. Step 1 makes $p_0$ a cokernel of $d^{-1}$; preservation of cokernels makes $V(p_0)$ a cokernel of $V(d^{-1})$. Therefore the induced $H^0(V(a)):H^0(V(P))\to V(M)$ is the unique comparison of these two cokernels and is invertible. Taking $H^0$ of the normalized equality in step 2 yields $c_M=H^0(V(a))\circ H^0(i_M)$, so the specified canonical map $c_M$ is an isomorphism.

source.place: Duals of Tag 05TC, lemma-negative-vanishing (1), and Tag 05TD, lemma-left-exact-higher-derived (3); direct cokernel calculation on the projective resolution.

proof.text: For $f:M\to N$, apply naturality of $\varepsilon$ to $f[0]$ and then apply $H^0$. On the source this is $T^0(f)$ by definition, and on the target the natural identification $H^0(V(M)[0])\cong V(M)$ sends the map of single complexes to $V(f)$. The resulting equation is exactly $c_N\circ T^0(f)=V(f)\circ c_M$.

source.place: Tag 05TD, lemma-left-exact-higher-derived (3), canonical natural comparison; cohomology functoriality.

proof.text: If $\varepsilon_{M[0]}$ is invertible, its image under each $H^q$ is invertible, and $H^q(V(M)[0])=0$ for $q<0$, so $T^q(M)=0$ in all negative degrees. Conversely, suppose all these negative-degree objects vanish. The isomorphism $i_M$ makes $H^q(V(P))=0$ for $q<0$. Thus $V(a):V(P)\to V(M)[0]$ induces isomorphisms on negative cohomology (both objects are zero), on degree zero by step 3, and on positive cohomology by the support calculation in step 3. It is therefore a quasi-isomorphism, by definition. The localization $Q_{\mathcal B}$ inverts it. Step 2 expresses $\varepsilon_{M[0]}$ as the composite of this isomorphism with $i_M$, proving the reverse implication.
